title: CoMAS: Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems via Interaction Rewards
claim: Prior self-evolution methods derive rewards from external verifiers or a single agent's intrinsic signals; ours derives them from multi-agent interaction.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right contrast, vertical flows, dashed dividers, right column expanded
description: Three vertical columns separated by dashed lines compare reward sources for RL-based LLM self-evolution. Each column starts with a blue Question box feeding an agent. The left column (External Rewards) and middle column (Intrinsic Rewards) are nearly identical stacks: yellow outputs o1..oG, a gray box, purple rewards r1..rG, then pink advantages A1..AG. The left gray box shows a scale and a graph icon labeled Rule-Based Verifier and Specialized Reward Model. The middle gray box lists Certainty/Confidence, Semantic Entropy and Pseudo-Labels (Voting). The right column (Ours) is larger. It shows a Multi-Agent System with several model logos and a nested discussion in which agents post solutions (green) and evaluations (red). Thumbs up and thumbs down icons in purple reward boxes come from those evaluations, then feed into the pink advantages. The eye goes first to the busy right column.
caption: A comparison of our proposed CoMAS framework with existing RL-based self-evolution methods. The left column outlines methods utilizing external rewards from verifiers or reward models. The middle column outlines methods leveraging intrinsic rewards from metrics such as self-certainty, confidence, semantic entropy, and pseudo-labels from majority voting. The right column outlines our CoMAS framework, which derives rewards from multi-agent interactions.
abstract: Self-evolution is a central research topic in enabling large language model (LLM)-based agents to continually improve their capabilities after pretraining. Recent research has witnessed a transition from reinforcement learning (RL)-free to RL-based methods. Current RL-based methods either rely on dense external reward signals or extract intrinsic reward signals from LLMs themselves. However, these approaches diverge from the self-evolution mechanisms observed in human intelligence, where individuals learn and improve through mutual discussion and collaboration. In this work, we introduce Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems (CoMAS), a novel framework that enables agents to improve autonomously by learning from inter-agent interactions without external supervision. CoMAS generates intrinsic rewards from rich discussion dynamics, employs an LLM-as-a-judge mechanism to formulate these rewards, and optimizes each agent's policy through RL, thereby enabling decentralized and scalable co-evolution. Experimental results demonstrate that CoMAS consistently outperforms untrained agents and achieves state-of-the-art performance across most evaluation settings. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of interaction-based reward signals and reveal promising scalability as the number and diversity of agents increase. These findings establish CoMAS as a novel and effective paradigm for self-evolution in LLM-based agents.
